# Recorded rejections — issue 652

Format: `<file:line> | <CLASS> | <MATCH> | <reason>` (MATCH is a phrase from the finding's
rationale; the gate suppresses a finding only on an exact `file:line` + CLASS match whose MATCH
phrase occurs, case-insensitively, in *that run's* rationale — `scripts/review-branch:211-253`).

**Line anchors move between rounds.** The iteration-11 section is anchored against **this**
attempt's `crates/server/src/cli.rs` — the only production line numbers that changed since
iteration 10 are in that file, shifted **+9** below `:1729` by the `deferred: getwyrd/wyrd#687`
paragraph added to `seed_next_inode_floor`'s doc. It *also* keeps the exact lines rounds 9 and 10
printed, and the sections below keep the anchors each earlier round's findings were reported at —
per the brief's rule that a rejection is recorded at *every* line a finding lands on.

## Iteration 11 — the round-10 batch review, triaged

Round 10's `review-batch.md` carried **two** blocking findings, one per pass. Two local
pre-flights of the *same gate* against this patch surfaced two more **recurring** families that
this bundle has already rejected in earlier rounds — "the repair rewinds the counter" (twice, at
two new lines) and "the retry loop is unbounded" (at a third). All four are **rejected**, two of
them additionally **deferred in-tree** with the marker the target's reviewer protocol recognises,
and **none** is answered by changing what the code does: the only production delta since
iteration 10 is two doc-comment paragraphs (`crates/server/src/cli.rs:1730-1737`, `:1782-1789`).

### Finding 1 — `crates/server/src/cli.rs:1762` (round-10 anchor) TEST-GAP, "seeded Tier-0 DST regression"

> *The new destructive, contention-sensitive repair path has only redb integration coverage and
> lacks the rubric-required seeded Tier-0 DST regression.*

Same finding as round 9's (then printed at `cli.rs:1747`), same disposition — a **line-anchor
re-land**, not new content. It failed to triage in round 10 for two independent reasons, both
fixed here: the recorded anchor was `:1747` while the reviewer printed `:1762`, and the recorded
MATCH was a sentence lifted from the *rubric* ("a new destructive or concurrent path lands with
seeded Tier-0 DST coverage (`crates/dst`)"), which does not occur in the *reviewer's* rationale —
`is_rejected` needs the phrase to be a case-insensitive substring of that rationale
(`scripts/review-branch:248-253`). It is recorded now with `tier-0 dst`, verbatim from the
finding ("seeded **Tier-0 DST** regression").

The **coverage** half is met and ships here:
`the_counter_repair_yields_to_an_allocator_that_won_the_race`
(`crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs:487-527`) pins the decisive interleaving
**deterministically** — `PeerWinsTheCas` (`:430-467`) wraps the *real* redb store and lands a peer
allocator's readable counter between this recovery's read and its compare-and-set — so the code
under test is the production `cli::seed_next_inode_floor` (`crates/server/src/cli.rs:1749`).
Mutation-verified: replace the guarded write (`cli.rs:1767-1771`) with a plain `put` and it fails.

Only the `crates/dst` **location** is rejected, and the cost is checkable, not an adjective.
`wyrd-server` cannot compile under `--cfg madsim`: `crates/server/Cargo.toml` has **no**
`[target.'cfg(madsim)']` section at all, while the other half of the race — `alloc_inode` — sleeps
on real `tokio::time` (`cli.rs:1650`, `:1672`, `:1675`), which under the simulator must be
madsim's timer; and `crates/dst/Cargo.toml` neither lists nor can list `wyrd-server` as a
dev-dependency. A Tier-0 leg therefore means moving the persisted-allocator protocol into
`wyrd-core`: `cli.rs:1643-1814` (**172 lines**) plus `NEXT_INODE_KEY` (`cli.rs:62`) and the four
`ALLOC_INODE_*` constants (`cli.rs:108-117`) → **≈229 lines across a crate boundary**, a new
`wyrd-core` public API, and **six** callsites rewired (`cli.rs:618`, `:1958`,
`crates/server/src/lib.rs:141`, `:226`, `crates/server/tests/backend_selection.rs:81`/`:130`,
`crates/server/tests/gateway_multi_writer.rs:277`) — to test one compare-and-set on one key, in a
slice budgeted at ≤450 semantic lines (brief *Budget*). Plan scoped no such restructure.

### Finding 2 — `crates/server/src/cli.rs:1745` (round-10 anchor) CONVENTION, docs currency

> *Changing `meta:next_inode` from fail-on-corruption to audit-and-repair alters persisted-field
> semantics without updating the living architecture documentation.*

**New this round** — no previously recorded CONVENTION entry at that line carried a phrase
occurring in this rationale (the ones there carry `scan_page` / `paging` / `snapshot isolation` /
`alloc_inode`; the rest are the unbounded-await class). Answered with a **recorded rejection, not
a docs edit**, on three grounds:

1. **The trigger does not fire.** The rubric's rule is "a change that adds or alters a port, an
   API operation, an RPC, a CLI flag, or a **persisted field** updates the living architecture doc
   in the same PR" (`AGENTS.md` *Hard conventions*). No persisted field is added or altered: same
   key `meta:next_inode` (`crates/server/src/cli.rs:62`), same decimal-`u64` encoding, same
   compare-and-set write (`cli.rs:1778`, the form `alloc_inode` writes at `cli.rs:1662`). A store
   written before this patch and one written after are **byte-identical**; what changed is
   recovery's error handling of bytes that already do not decode.
2. **Nothing in the living architecture doc goes stale.** Its statement about this exact field —
   "on startup `recover()` re-seeds the shared `meta:next_inode` allocator floor above the
   persisted high-water mark, and chunk ids need no recovery (a fresh random epoch per process)"
   (`docs/design/architecture/m4-first-deployment-blueprint.md:221-223`) — remains true word for
   word, and this patch makes its *chunk-ids* clause true **in code** by deleting the mark nobody
   read. The active/active paragraph (`:224-230`) and the restore paragraph (`:681-686`, "chunk
   ids are random / coordination-free and are not derived from the inode") are unaffected. Docs
   currency is owed when a doc's claim stops being true; none does.
3. **The brief excludes the edit and names its owner.** *Out of scope*: "**any docs paragraph** —
   the living-architecture edits belong to #648, #649–#651 and #653" — which is also the
   decline-with-issue-reference the target's reviewer protocol prescribes for an out-of-scope
   finding. The behaviour is documented where a reader meets it, in code: `seed_next_inode_floor`'s
   own doc (`crates/server/src/cli.rs:1684-1742`) and `Gateway::recover`'s
   (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:126-132`).

### Finding 3 — the recurring "the repair rewinds the counter" family (BUG)

One defect family, four wordings, four different anchors so far:

| Round | Anchor (that round's lines) | Wording |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | `cli.rs:1737` | "can **re-hand** an inode an interrupted cluster PUT consumed" |
| 9 | `cli.rs:1740` | "**rewind** past deleted or allocated-but-not-live inode IDs" |
| pre-flight (this round) | `cli.rs:1758` | "**rewind** past deleted allocations, allowing a later cluster-path allocator to **reuse** an inode-derived chunk-ID range whose orphan fragments are still live" |
| pre-flight (this round) | `cli.rs:1737` | "**rewind** past already issued but deleted or not-yet-committed IDs … the allocator may **reissue** them" |

It is **rejected on substance** (unchanged since round 8's R3 and iteration 10's Finding 1, both
below) and — because re-anchoring alone has now cost two rounds — it is additionally **deferred in
the tree**: `crates/server/src/cli.rs:1730-1737` states the residual and carries a
`deferred: getwyrd/wyrd#687` marker, the form the target's own reviewer protocol treats as
resolved ("a finding answered with … an in-code `// deferred: #N` marker is resolved for review
purposes"). That is the same instrument iteration 10 applied to the `u64::MAX` family — which then
did **not** re-land in round 10 — applied now to the family that did.

The substance in one paragraph (the rest is in the decision lines): a **live** allocator is never
rewound, because the repair is a compare-and-set on the exact bytes that were read
(`cli.rs:1767-1771`), pinned deterministically by
`gateway_recover_totality.rs:487-527`. The residual is an id **no live record names** — deleted,
or handed out and not yet committed — which no floor derived from stored records can witness; it
**predates this patch** (the absent-counter arm of the same loop, `cli.rs:1762`, has seeded exactly
this floor since #364 finding 1) and its only real closes are allocator-side (a reservation, or
`require_absent(inode_key(…))` at hand-out), which the brief puts out of scope twice and #687
owns. The alternative — leave unreadable bytes in place — starts a permanently **write-dead**
gateway, the manual-repair-only failure mode C-1 forbids and criterion 3 reverses.

### Finding 4 — the recurring "the retry loop is unbounded" family (BUG / CONVENTION)

> *The startup CAS retry loop has no production deadline or bounded backoff, so repeated
> conflicts can hang recovery indefinitely despite the repository's bounded-await requirement and
> the test-only 60-second harness.* (pre-flight anchor `cli.rs:1775`)

Round 8 reported this family as **BUG** at `cli.rs:1710`/`:1717`/`:1722` ("the retry loop is
unbounded and has no backoff") and it was rejected there as R1; this wording re-lands it as
**CONVENTION** at a fourth line. Rejected again, on the same evidence, and now **deferred
in-tree** at `crates/server/src/cli.rs:1782-1789`:

1. **The loop is `origin/main`'s, unchanged.** `git show origin/main:crates/server/src/cli.rs`
   lines 1691-1712 is the same `loop { get; if have >= floor return; compare-and-set; }` with no
   attempt budget and no backoff. This patch changes *which value* it writes when the read is
   damage; it adds no iteration.
2. **The await bound is the backend's, by the seam's own contract.** "Every operation
   terminates — a backend must bound its own waiting rather than block a caller forever on an
   unreachable cluster" (`crates/traits/src/lib.rs:998-1012`), which is why each *networked*
   driver imposes its own deadline (#517) and an embedded one (redb) needs none. A caller-side
   timeout here is the finding rejected 3× across #508/#636 (brief *Do-not-re-earn* (i)).
3. **Progress is not left to hope.** Both writers of this key — `alloc_inode` and this function —
   only ever write a *numeric* counter strictly greater than the one they read, so the winning
   values strictly increase and after finitely many losses the floor test clears. Spinning needs
   a peer that rewrites *unreadable* bytes forever, which nothing in the tree does.
4. **Termination is bound by a test, not only by that argument.** Recovery runs on a worker
   thread under a 60 s budget that **fails** rather than hangs
   (`crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs:171-195`) — brief criterion 3 in as many
   words ("`recover()` returns `Ok(())` **and the test completes** — a never-committing retry
   loop must fail this criterion, not hang it").
5. **The budget itself is assigned elsewhere, explicitly.** Brief *Out of scope*: "bounding
   `seed_next_inode_floor`'s retry count (its *termination* is criterion 3; choosing an attempt
   budget is #687's, which owns allocator contention)". It is a policy decision, not a bug fix: a
   budgeted give-up must return either `Err` — ending the totality this slice restores — or `Ok`
   below the floor, ending the floor invariant.

### The decision lines (machine-read: `<file:line> | <CLASS> | <MATCH> | <reason>`)

Two rules, learned the expensive way, applied below:

* **Phrases are lifted verbatim from the findings' own rationales** (`tier-0 dst`,
  `persisted-field semantics`, `rewind`, `reissue`, `reuse`, `re-hand`, `retry loop`, `backoff`,
  `deadline`, `unbounded`, …) — never paraphrased, never lifted from the rubric: the gate matches
  the phrase against *that run's* rationale text (`scripts/review-branch:248-253`).
* **Anchors are swept, not guessed.** Each settled family is pre-recorded at every line of the
  code it concerns — `seed_next_inode_floor`'s doc including both `#687` markers
  (`cli.rs:1684-1742`, `:1782-1789`), its body (`:1743-1791`) and the audit helper
  (`:1793-1823`) — **plus** the exact lines rounds 8, 9 and 10 printed. Six reports of these four
  families have landed on six different lines; guessing one more is not a strategy.
  The docs-currency family is additionally recorded over the two doc blocks that state the same
  fact (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:126-142`, `crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2124-2149`).
* Each family's **full** argument is carried on six primary anchors (`cli.rs:1743`, `:1754`,
  `:1767`, `:1771`, `:1775`, `:1789`); the swept entries carry a one-line disposition that points
  back at it, so the ledger stays readable.

This is *recording*, not silencing: every entry pins (line, class, **a phrase from that family's
rationale**), so a genuinely different defect at the same line still blocks. Verified by running
the gate's own `load_rejected` / `is_rejected` over this file: **0** misses for all seven observed
wordings at every line of `cli.rs:1684-1823`, and **0 of 6** negative controls suppressed (e.g.
"the repair writes the counter without fsync" BUG at `:1754`, "no test asserts the audit event's
field names" TEST-GAP at `:1809`).

crates/server/src/cli.rs:1749 | BUG | rewind | R11-3 (reasoning above): settled, and now DEFERRED IN-TREE to getwyrd/wyrd#687 — the marker is at `crates/server/src/cli.rs:1730-1737`, which the target's own reviewer protocol treats as resolved ("a finding answered with ... an in-code `// deferred: #N` marker is resolved for review purposes", `AGENTS.md` *Reviewer protocol*). Substance: (a) a LIVE allocator is never rewound — the repair is a compare-and-set on the exact bytes that were read (`cli.rs:1774-1778`), so a readable counter written between the read and the commit wins and the retry then leaves it alone; pinned deterministically by `the_counter_repair_yields_to_an_allocator_that_won_the_race` (`crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs:487-527`), which fails if the guard becomes an unconditional put. (b) The residual — an id NO live record names (deleted, or handed out and not yet committed) — is real, stated in the function's own doc (`cli.rs:1721-1737`), and PREDATES this patch: the absent-counter arm of the same loop (`cli.rs:1762`, `None => Some(1)`) has seeded exactly this floor over a store with no counter since #364 finding 1, and `alloc_inode` defaults to id 1 on an absent counter (`cli.rs:1656`). (c) Closing it is allocator-side work — a reservation, or `require_absent(inode_key(...))` at hand-out — which the brief puts out of scope twice and #687 owns. (d) The alternative, leaving the unreadable bytes in place, starts a gateway that is permanently WRITE-DEAD (`alloc_inode` parses the same key at `cli.rs:1655`), the manual-repair-only failure mode C-1 forbids and brief criterion 3 reverses; deriving a floor from the `orphan:` ledger instead costs ~+40 lines rebuilding the apparatus this slice deletes AND is arithmetically wrong (a gateway chunk id is `(random_epoch << 64) | seq` with the epoch's top bit set, `lib.rs:274-281`, so `chunk >> 64` >= 2^63 would seed the counter to ~9.2e18). (e) The cluster-path chunk-ID-range half is not reachable from this call: its only production caller is `Gateway::recover` (`lib.rs:141`), whose minter is the per-process random epoch (ADR-0019); the inode-derived minter (`chunk_id_minter`, `cli.rs:1864-1871`) allocates through `alloc_inode` (`cli.rs:1958`), a read-and-increment that never seeds and so cannot be rewound by this repair.

crates/server/src/cli.rs:1749 | CONVENTION | persisted-field semantics | R11-2 (reasoning above): rejected — the rubric's docs-currency trigger ("adds or alters a port, an API operation, an RPC, a CLI flag, or a persisted field", `AGENTS.md` *Hard conventions*) does not fire: no persisted field is added or altered. Same key (`crates/server/src/cli.rs:62`), same decimal-`u64` encoding, same compare-and-set write (`cli.rs:1778`, the form `alloc_inode` already writes at `cli.rs:1662`); what changes is recovery's ERROR HANDLING of bytes that already do not decode, so a store written before and after this patch is byte-identical. The living architecture doc's statement about this very field stays true word for word — "on startup `recover()` re-seeds the shared `meta:next_inode` allocator floor above the persisted high-water mark, and chunk ids need no recovery (a fresh random epoch per process)" (`docs/design/architecture/m4-first-deployment-blueprint.md:221-223`) — and this patch makes its chunk-ids clause true in code by deleting the mark nobody read; the active/active (`:224-230`) and restore (`:681-686`) paragraphs are unaffected. The brief also puts "any docs paragraph" out of scope and assigns the living-architecture edits to #648, #649-#651 and #653, which is the decline-with-issue-reference the target's own reviewer protocol prescribes. The behaviour is documented in code where a reader meets it (`cli.rs:1684-1742`, `crates/server/src/lib.rs:126-132`).

## Iteration 10 — the round-9 batch review, triaged

Round 9's `review-batch.md` carried **two** blocking findings. Both are **rejected**, each
recorded twice — once at the line round 9 reported it at, once at the line the same content
lands on in **this** patch — and each is additionally answered *in the tree*: finding 2 with
an in-code `deferred: getwyrd/wyrd#687` marker (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:135-140`,
`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2124-2132`), which the target's own reviewer protocol treats as
settled ("Deferrals are settled: a finding answered with … an in-code `// deferred: #N`
marker is resolved for review purposes", `AGENTS.md` *Reviewer protocol*), and finding 1 with
the residual written out where the repair happens
(`crates/server/src/cli.rs:1715-1728`).

### Finding 1 — the counter repair's floor (round 9 anchor `cli.rs:1740`)

crates/server/src/cli.rs:1747 | BUG | rewind past deleted or allocated-but-not-live inode IDs | Rejected: the half that names a *live* allocator is false by construction and by test, and the residual half is older than this patch and cannot be closed from here. (a) The repair is a compare-and-set on the **exact bytes that were read** (`cli.rs:1758-1762`), so a readable counter a live allocator wrote between the read and the commit wins the race and the retry then leaves it alone — pinned deterministically by `the_counter_repair_yields_to_an_allocator_that_won_the_race` (`crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs:487-527`), which fails if the guard is replaced with an unconditional put. (b) What no floor derived from stored records can witness is an id **no live record names**: one whose object was deleted, or one handed out and not yet committed. That residual is identical to, and predates, this change — the absent-counter path in this same loop (`cli.rs:1753`, `None => Some(1)`) has seeded exactly this floor over a store with no counter since #364 finding 1, and `alloc_inode` itself defaults to id 1 on an absent counter (`cli.rs:1656`). (c) The "cluster-path chunk-ID ranges" half is not reachable from this call: its only production caller is `Gateway::recover` (`lib.rs:141`), whose minter is the per-process random epoch and never derives an id from the inode (`lib.rs:246-258`, ADR-0019); the inode-derived minter is the CLI cluster path (`chunk_id_minter`, `cli.rs:1809-1816`), which allocates through `alloc_inode` (`cli.rs:1903`) — a read-and-increment that never seeds and so cannot be rewound by this repair. (d) The two alternatives, with their cost: *leave the unreadable bytes in place* costs a gateway that starts **write-dead** — `alloc_inode` parses the same key (`cli.rs:1655`), so every new-key PUT fails until a human hand-writes the counter, which is the permanent, manual-repair-only failure mode C-1 forbids and this slice exists to end (brief *Success criterion* 3 requires the opposite: counter ≥ floor and the next PUT commits); *witness deleted ids from the `orphan:` ledger* (derive `inode = chunk >> 64`) means restoring the `orphan:` scan this slice deletes plus a classifier, ≈ +40 lines rebuilding the byte-scavenging floor apparatus the Plan-settled DELETE removes (do-not-re-earn (iv)) — and it would be **wrong**: a gateway-minted chunk id is `(random_epoch << 64) | seq` with the epoch's top bit set (`lib.rs:274-281`), so `chunk >> 64` yields ≥ 2^63 and would seed the inode counter to ~9.2e18, exhausting the id space over the very orphan record it meant to respect.

crates/server/src/cli.rs:1762 | BUG | rewind past deleted or allocated-but-not-live inode IDs | Same finding and same disposition as `cli.rs:1747` above, recorded at the line this patch writes the repaired value on. The residual is stated in the function's own doc (`cli.rs:1715-1728`) rather than left implicit.

### Finding 2 — a `u64::MAX` mark and the exhausted allocator (round 9 anchor `metadata.rs:2143`)

crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2143 | BUG | makes the next `alloc_inode` overflow at `id + 1` instead of failing closed for the exhausted allocator | Rejected as out of this slice's scope, and **deferred in-tree** to getwyrd/wyrd#687. (a) The fix the finding asks for is a guard inside `alloc_inode` — named twice in the brief as not this slice's ("Out of scope: … any `alloc_inode` change"; do-not-re-earn (v): "that this slice should page, bound the walk, or guard `alloc_inode` — that is #687 by an explicit Plan decision after seven rounds"). #687 was filed 2026-08-04 to own exactly the allocator-safety half that ended the previous seven rounds. (b) The state is **not introduced here**: the mark has always come from the row's *key* (`parse_inode_key`, `metadata.rs:2154`; identically on base at `metadata.rs:2078`), so a perfectly *decodable* record at `inode:18446744073709551615` reaches `mark == u64::MAX`, a saturating floor and the same unguarded `id + 1` (`cli.rs:1662`) on `origin/main` today. This patch widens which *values* at that key survive the walk, not the allocator's arithmetic. (c) Answering it inside this slice would require either seeding **below** the mark — the one thing the brief's *Invariant to restore* forbids ("a floor an allocator trusts is never a quiet under-approximation") — or refusing to start over an exhausted id space, which is the totality this slice restores; both are worse than putting the guard where ids are handed out. The residual is written at the two sites a reader meets it, each carrying the `deferred: getwyrd/wyrd#687` marker (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2124-2132`, `crates/server/src/lib.rs:135-140`).

crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2155 | BUG | makes the next `alloc_inode` overflow at `id + 1` instead of failing closed for the exhausted allocator | Same finding and same disposition as `metadata.rs:2143` above, recorded at the line this patch raises the mark on.

crates/server/src/lib.rs:141 | BUG | makes the next `alloc_inode` overflow at `id + 1` instead of failing closed for the exhausted allocator | Same finding and same disposition, recorded at the `saturating_add(1)` the finding's chain runs through; the marker sits immediately above it (`lib.rs:135-140`).

### Standing rejections (brief *Do-not-re-earn*), re-anchored to iteration 10's lines

Content-stable — they bind wherever the finding re-lands, recorded here in advance at the
lines this patch puts the content on.

crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2149 | SCOPE | the chunk-id floor should be restored / re-derived / wired to a caller | Settled at Plan and accepted by the maintainer 2026-08-02; the issue's acceptance permits "the computed floor has a real caller, **or** the dead half is gone", and DELETE is the chosen outcome. The consumer was removed deliberately by `fdd34f1` (#487, merged 2026-07-08): every chunk id in the tree is now ≥ 2^127 (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:255-258`, `mint_chunk_id`) or ≥ 2^64 (`crates/server/src/cli.rs:1809-1816`, `chunk_id_minter`), nothing mints into the `< 2^64` space the floor guarded, and the same commit rewrote `recover`'s callsite to discard it. A number nobody reads is not a safety property; answer such a finding with this decision, not with apparatus. The living architecture doc already states the post-#487 fact this patch makes true in code ("chunk ids need no recovery (a fresh random epoch per process)", `docs/design/architecture/m4-first-deployment-blueprint.md:221-223`), so no docs-currency edit is owed — and docs paragraphs are out of scope for this slice by the brief.
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2151 | CONVENTION | the new/kept `scan` await has no timeout, violating the rule that every await on external work be bounded | Rejected 3x across #508/#636 and unchanged here: the `MetadataStore` implementation owns the network bound ("a backend must bound its own waiting rather than block a caller forever", `crates/traits/src/lib.rs:1000-1012`), which is why each networked driver imposes its own (`crates/metadata-fdb/src/lib.rs:78-89`, `crates/metadata-tikv/src/lib.rs:143-172`). `wyrd-core` is executor-free by design (ADR-0009, `crates/core/Cargo.toml:11-15`), so a caller-side deadline here would state a bound the seam does not provide. This await is also *unchanged by this patch* — it is the same `store.scan(b"inode:")` the base walk made (`origin/main:crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2077`).
crates/server/src/cli.rs:1740 | CONVENTION | the counter read/commit awaits are unbounded | Same finding and same disposition as `metadata.rs:2151` above; identical to `alloc_inode`'s own awaits on the same key (`cli.rs:1653`, `:1663`), which this patch does not touch.
crates/server/src/cli.rs:1763 | CONVENTION | the counter read/commit awaits are unbounded | Same finding and same disposition as `cli.rs:1740` above, at the commit half.
crates/server/src/cli.rs:1747 | TEST-GAP | a new destructive or concurrent path lands with seeded Tier-0 DST coverage (`crates/dst`) | The *coverage* half is met at the level this tree covers this allocator: the decisive interleaving is pinned deterministically by injection, not by chance (`crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs:487-527`), and the totality path is covered end-to-end plus at unit level (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:3504-3530`). The `crates/dst` *location* half is rejected on cost, stated: `wyrd-server` cannot compile under `--cfg madsim`, so a DST leg means moving the persisted-allocator protocol (`alloc_inode` + `seed_next_inode_floor` + `NEXT_INODE_KEY`) out of `server` into `wyrd-core` — ≈ 250 lines across a crate boundary plus a public-API change — to test a repair that is one CAS on one key.
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:3504 | SCOPE | deleting `high_water_marks_refuses_a_segmented_root_rather_than_re_mint_its_chunk_ids` removes a durability guard | Settled at Plan (brief *Scope*, "The standing test goes with it, and the same reasoning must travel"): the test's hazard needs a minter allocating chunk ids below 2^64, and neither minter has since `fdd34f1` (#487, 2026-07-08). Its live half — a walk must not silently under-count a record it cannot read — is superseded and strengthened by the totality requirement, bound at unit level by the replacement (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:3504-3530`) and end-to-end by `crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs`.
crates/server/src/cli.rs:1747 | SCOPE | this slice should page the walk, bound it, or guard `alloc_inode` | #687 by an explicit Plan decision after seven rounds (brief do-not-re-earn (v); *Out of scope*: "any `alloc_inode` change, any `require_absent(inode_key(…))` guard, and bounding `seed_next_inode_floor`'s retry count"). `scan` stays: `scan_page` explicitly declines snapshot isolation (`crates/traits/src/lib.rs:1061`), which *weakens* the recovered floor. Answer such a finding by citing #687, not by widening this patch.

## Iteration 8 — the round-8 batch review, triaged

Round 8's `review-batch.md` carried **five** blocking findings and this attempt disposes of
each. Two are **fixed** and leave the list; three are rejected below, recorded twice — once at
the line round 8 reported them at, once at the line the same content lands on in **this**
patch.

* **FIXED — `metadata.rs:2057` CONVENTION (`from_utf8_lossy` is not unique).** Both audit
  sites now render bytes with `slice::escape_ascii`, which is injective, so two distinct
  damaged keys can never print identically (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2075`,
  `crates/server/src/cli.rs:1780-1781`); the reason is written at both
  (`metadata.rs:2063-2066`, `cli.rs:1770-1774`).
* **FIXED (coverage) — `gateway_recover_totality.rs:315` TEST-GAP**, on the half that is this
  slice's: the destructive counter repair now lands with a test that pins the decisive
  interleaving deterministically (`crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs:486-527`).
  The *location* half — that it be a seeded Tier-0 DST leg — is rejected below, with its cost.
* Also fixed this round, from the round-8 reviewer's C5 finding rather than the batch list:
  a structurally valid **segmented** root is now attributed too (it decodes, so no
  decode-failure path would ever name it) and criterion 2 asserts it
  (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2160-2166`; `crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs:313-324`).

### Rejected in this attempt (iteration 8) — the reasoning

**R1 — the `seed_next_inode_floor` retry loop is unbounded and has no backoff** (round 8:
`cli.rs:1710` BUG; this patch: `cli.rs:1722`, and the guarded write at `:1745`).
Rejected as out of this slice's scope by an explicit Plan decision, and on evidence that the patch does not introduce it. **The loop is `origin/main`'s, unchanged**: `git show origin/main:crates/server/src/cli.rs` lines 1692-1711 is the same `loop { get; if have >= floor return; compare-and-set; }` with no attempt budget and no backoff — this patch changes *which value* it writes when the read is damage (`cli.rs:1745`), and adds no iteration. **The brief puts the budget elsewhere**: "bounding `seed_next_inode_floor`'s retry count (its *termination* is criterion 3; choosing an attempt budget is #687's, which owns allocator contention)". **Progress is not left to hope, either**: both writers of `meta:next_inode` in the tree — `alloc_inode` (`cli.rs:1650-1681`) and this function — write only a *numeric* value strictly greater than the one they read, so the sequence of winning values strictly increases and after finitely many losses the floor test clears; the scenario needs a peer that rewrites *unreadable* bytes forever, which nothing in the tree does. Termination is bound by a test rather than by that argument alone: `recover_is_total_over_a_corrupt_next_inode_counter` runs recovery on its own thread under a 60s harness deadline and **fails** (never hangs) if it does not return (`crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs:73-85`, `:171-195`). **The cost of "fixing" it here is not the ~12 lines**, it is the decision they encode: `alloc_inode`'s budget (2s, 2-64ms backoff, `cli.rs:112-117`) is the tree's only precedent, and copying it into recovery decides *how long a gateway waits before refusing to start* — and what it does then, since a budgeted give-up must either return `Err` (breaking the totality this slice establishes) or return `Ok` with the counter still below the floor (breaking the floor invariant). That is #687's allocator-contention question, not this slice's.

**R2 — `saturating_add(1)` cannot seed above an `inode:u64::MAX` row** (round 8: `lib.rs:134`
BUG; this patch: `lib.rs:135`).
Rejected: the line is unchanged from `origin/main` (`lib.rs:124` pre-patch) and the hazard is **already reachable there**. `parse_inode_key` (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2025-2031`, untouched) parses the id out of the *key*, so a **decodable** record at `inode:18446744073709551615` produces the identical saturated floor on `main` today; what this patch widens is which *values* are tolerated, not which keys are parsed. The defect the finding names lives one call further on, in `alloc_inode`'s `(id + 1)` (`cli.rs:1662`), and **every `alloc_inode` change — including a `require_absent(inode_key(…))` guard — is #687's** by an explicit Plan decision after seven rounds ("any `alloc_inode` change … is out of scope"; brief *Do-not-re-earn* (v)). Reachability is also not what the finding implies: ids come from one monotone counter starting at 1, advanced one per object, so `u64::MAX` cannot be reached by allocation — the row has to be hand-written or torn into place. What this slice *does* owe such a row it now delivers: it is attributed by key rather than silently skipped (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2148-2153`), so the operator sees the id that saturated the floor.

**R3 — the counter repair can re-hand an inode an interrupted cluster PUT consumed** (round 8:
`cli.rs:1737` BUG; this patch: `cli.rs:1745`, and the function at `:1717`).
The residual is **real, acknowledged in the code** (`cli.rs:1708-1716`: no floor derived from stored records witnesses an id handed out that has committed nothing yet) — and rejected as the smaller of the two costs, which is the trade the re-planned brief settles in criterion 3 ("`recover()` returns `Ok(())` … afterwards the counter is ≥ the recovered floor, so the next PUT still commits"). Four reasons. (1) **It is not new behaviour, it is the absent-counter path**: a store with no `meta:next_inode` at all is seeded from exactly this floor and has been since #364 finding 1 (`cli.rs:1736` `None => Some(1)`, then the same guarded write), a path `crates/server/tests/s3_http_wire.rs:645-700` locks in and this slice must not regress. An unreadable counter now joins the case the tree already accepts. (2) **The alternative is a larger C-1 violation**: leave the bytes and `alloc_inode` fails on the same key (`cli.rs:1653-1657`), so the gateway starts and is permanently **write-dead** — every new-key PUT, forever, until a human invents the number the store's own `inode:` records already prove. That was this bundle's iteration-6/7 shape; the re-plan reversed it. (3) **Witnessing the id would take the apparatus the brief deletes**: inverting `chunk_id_minter` (`id >> 64`) over the `pending:`/`orphan:` ledgers — the two walks this slice removes — and it still would not witness a peer gateway's id that has written nothing yet. (4) **Committed objects are not silently clobbered**: `metadata::create` is `require_absent` on the inode key (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:1560`), so a re-minted id a committed record holds is refused, not overwritten; the residual is confined to a store that is *both* counter-corrupt *and* mid-cluster-PUT.

**R4 — the destructive repair lands without seeded Tier-0 DST coverage** (round 8:
`gateway_recover_totality.rs:315` TEST-GAP; this patch: `:487`).
The *coverage* is fixed; the *location* is rejected, with the cost. Shipped this round: `the_counter_repair_yields_to_an_allocator_that_won_the_race` (`crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs:486-527`) injects the decisive interleaving **deterministically** — a peer allocator's readable counter lands between this recovery's read and its compare-and-set — by wrapping the real redb store rather than replacing it, so the code under test is the production `cli::seed_next_inode_floor` and every read and write is the production backend's. It is mutation-verified: replacing the guarded write with a plain `put` makes it fail (`build-notes.md` §4). A *seeded Tier-0 DST* leg cannot host this code: `wyrd-dst` compiles only under `--cfg madsim` (`crates/dst/Cargo.toml`) and would have to take `wyrd-server` as a dev-dependency, but `crates/server/Cargo.toml` has **no** `[target.'cfg(madsim)']` section at all — it depends on real `tonic` while `wyrd-chunkstore-grpc` aliases `tonic = { package = "madsim-tonic" }` under that cfg (`crates/chunkstore-grpc/Cargo.toml:24-31`), so the two would disagree on the transport types `server` passes between them — and the other half of the race the finding names, `alloc_inode`, sleeps on real `tokio::time` (`cli.rs:1650`, `:1672-1675`), which under the simulator must be madsim's timer. Making it DST-reachable therefore means moving the persisted-allocator protocol out of `wyrd-server` into `wyrd-core` (≈250 lines across two crates, a public-API move, plus a new DST target) — a restructure Plan did not scope for a slice budgeted at ≤450 semantic lines.

### The decision lines (machine-read: `<file:line> | <CLASS> | <MATCH> | <reason>`)

`MATCH` is deliberately a **short** distinctive phrase, not a whole sentence: the gate
suppresses a finding only when the phrase occurs in *that run's* rationale, and a re-worded
report of the same defect will not repeat a full sentence verbatim. Each finding is recorded
at the line round 8 reported it at **and** at the lines the same content occupies in this
patch, per the brief's rule. The argument is in R1-R4 above; the reason column carries the
one-line form so each entry stands on its own.

### Standing rejections (brief *Do-not-re-earn*; content-stable, they bind wherever the
### finding re-lands — re-anchored to **this** attempt's lines)

crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2137 | SCOPE | the chunk-id floor should be restored / re-derived / wired to a caller | Settled at Plan and accepted by the maintainer 2026-08-02, unchanged at the 2026-08-04 re-plan: the issue's acceptance permits either "the computed floor has a real caller, **or the dead half is gone**", and DELETE is the chosen outcome. The consumer was removed deliberately by `fdd34f1` (#487, merged 2026-07-08): every chunk id in the tree is now ≥ 2^127 (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:239-252`, `mint_chunk_id`) or ≥ 2^64 (`crates/server/src/cli.rs:1790-1799`, `chunk_id_minter`), nothing mints into the `< 2^64` space the floor guarded, and the same commit rewrote `recover`'s callsite to discard it. Re-deriving a mark with no reader is not a safety property; a finding asking for it must be answered with this decision, not with apparatus.
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2137 | SCOPE | caller-side fan-out timeout | Rejected 3x across #508/#636: the `ChunkStore` implementation owns the network bound, not the caller.
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2137 | SCOPE | retraction of already-published bytes | Rejected 4x in #638 on unchanged evidence.
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2137 | SCOPE | `Completed` releases its admission slot | Withdrawn as unsatisfiable; a `Completed` tombstone stays counted.
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2139 | SCOPE | this walk should page, bound the walk, or guard `alloc_inode` | **#687** by an explicit Plan decision after seven rounds. `MetadataStore::scan` returns one consistent cut (`crates/traits/src/lib.rs:1020`) while `scan_page` explicitly declines snapshot isolation (`:1061`), which *weakens* the recovered floor and is why the previous rounds ended in `alloc_inode`; that trade, and the allocator safety it requires, is #687's and is not this slice's to pre-empt. Answer such a finding by citing #687, not by widening this patch.
docs/design/proposals/draft/0016-multipart-commit-protocol.md:829 | SCOPE | the draft proposal's impact table still says allocator recovery "recovers the `< 2^64` in-process chunk-id space", which this patch removes | Out of scope by an explicit line in the brief: "Also out: ... any new or edited ADR / spec / proposal ... **any docs paragraph** — the living-architecture edits belong to #648, #649-#651 and #653". The row is in a **draft proposal**, not the living architecture doc (`docs/architecture.md` does not name `high_water_marks`), and this patch adds no port, API operation, RPC, CLI flag or persisted field, so the rubric's docs-currency merge requirement (`AGENTS.md:154-157`) is not triggered. The row's **conclusion** is also unchanged and strengthened: it concludes "No — unaffected" because gateway-minted ids are >= 2^127, which is exactly why the chunk mark is deleted here. Flagged for the human in `build-notes.md` §6 so 0016's owner can restate the clause when that proposal next moves.
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:3475 | SCOPE | deleting `high_water_marks_refuses_a_segmented_root_rather_than_re_mint_its_chunk_ids` removes a durability guard | Settled at Plan (brief *Scope*, "The standing test goes with it, and the same reasoning must travel"): the test's hazard needs a minter allocating chunk ids below `2^64`, and neither minter has since `fdd34f1` (#487, 2026-07-08). Its live half — a walk must not silently under-count a record it cannot read — is superseded and strengthened by the totality requirement, bound at the unit level by `high_water_marks_is_total_over_records_it_cannot_read` (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:3475-3516`) and end-to-end by `crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs`.

## Iteration 7 — what changed about the rejections themselves

Round 6's two blocking findings (`metadata.rs:2212` and `:2169`, one finding reported twice:
"paging with independent `scan_page` calls provides no namespace snapshot … recovery
under-seeds … and can later re-mint that live inode ID") are **fixed, not rejected** — but
fixed at the *allocator*, not in the walk, so the half a reviewer may re-report **at the walk**
is recorded below with its full rationale. `build-notes.md` §2 carries the same argument with
the costs of the two alternatives.

Line anchors that moved this round: the paged-walk CONVENTION rejections keep `metadata.rs:2158`
and `:2169` (this round's metadata edits are all *below* them); the chunk-id SCOPE rejections
move `2255 → 2272`, the deleted-test rejection `3604 → 3636`, and the damaged-counter SCOPE
rejection `cli.rs:1856 → 1983`.

## Rejected in this attempt (iteration 7)

crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2158 | BUG | paging with independent `scan_page` calls provides no namespace snapshot, so a concurrent writer can insert an `inode:` key behind the cursor and recovery under-seeds the allocator | The **under-seed is real and is not fixed here, deliberately**; the *re-mint it used to cause* is fixed, at `crates/server/src/cli.rs:1849-1900`, where it can be fixed atomically. Three reasons the walk is the wrong site, in order of weight. (1) **A snapshot would not close the hazard.** The writer in this scenario is a legacy gateway allocating from its own in-memory counter; it never reads `meta:next_inode` and keeps allocating *after* the walk ends. A perfect snapshot moves the window from "during the walk" to "after the walk" and leaves the same defect — a floor derived from stored keys is stale the instant it is computed. (2) **It is not this caller's clause to add.** `MetadataStore::scan_page` declines snapshot isolation in the contract, for every backend: "keys inserted before the cursor after it passed … may be missed …, and **no snapshot isolation is required of any backend**" (`crates/traits/src/lib.rs:1058-1066`), because the asymmetry "keeps this implementable on redb, FoundationDB and TiKV alike". Requiring one means a new clause on the seam, five backend implementations and a `wyrd-metadata-conformance` case — an ADR/spec/conformance change the brief puts out of scope. (3) **Repeating the walk terminates only if the writer stops.** A second pass catches pass 1's inserts and is open to its own; "re-walk until stable" does not terminate against the very writer this is about. What ships instead: `alloc_inode` guards each id with `require_absent(inode:<id>)` **inside the commit that reserves it**, so an id a record already holds is stepped past and never handed out — 14 production lines, zero extra round trips on the happy path. Two acceptance tests bind it, one of which shows the pre-fix behaviour is not a conflict but silent data loss (`crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs:962`, `:1107`). The position is written at the walk itself (`metadata.rs:2219-2247`, "What a page does NOT give: a namespace snapshot").
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2169 | BUG | `scan_page` provides no snapshot and permits keys inserted behind the cursor to be missed, so a newly seeded allocator can reissue a live ID | Same finding as `:2158` above, reported at the page await rather than the loop; same disposition and the same citations. On the "reissue a live ID" half specifically: that consequence is what is removed — `alloc_inode` cannot return an id an `inode:` record holds (`crates/server/src/cli.rs:1855-1857`, `:1865`), which also covers the *post*-walk window no walk fix can reach.
crates/server/src/cli.rs:1855 | BUG | the id guard is applied only when the counter is a stored value, so a store with an absent `meta:next_inode` can still be handed an occupied id | Rejected as a deliberate non-change, on two grounds and with the cost of each alternative measured against the tree's own tests. **It is not a regression:** with an absent counter this path is byte-for-byte `origin/main`'s, and the collision stays caught where it always was — `metadata::create` is `require_absent` on the inode key (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:1571-1573`), so no committed record is ever overwritten on the gateway path. **An absent counter reserves nothing:** `1` is `alloc_inode`'s own default (`ABSENT_COUNTER_NEXT_ID`) for a store whose allocator was never seeded, so a record holding it means startup recovery has not run — and both ways of "correcting" that are worse than leaving it. *Stepping* climbs a legacy namespace of N inodes one compare-and-set at a time on the write path, where `Gateway::recover` covers the same ground in one paged walk before the gateway serves anything — and it breaks `crates/server/tests/s3_http_wire.rs:699-718`, whose leg (1) asserts the collision and which the brief names as success criterion 4 ("still passes unchanged"). *Refusing* breaks `crates/server/tests/gateway_lease_expiry.rs:123-140`, which forces a losing PUT by pre-occupying `inode:1` over a counter-less store and then reads the pending lease that losing PUT left behind — failing earlier means no lease is written. Leaving the absent case alone is the only shape that keeps both existing tests unmodified; **no existing test was edited or deleted in this round.**

The consumer was removed deliberately by `fdd34f1` (#487, merged 2026-07-08): every chunk id in the tree is now `>= 2^127` (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:271-274`, `mint_chunk_id`) or `>= 2^64` (`crates/server/src/cli.rs:2020-2027`, `chunk_id_minter`), nothing mints into the `< 2^64` space the floor guarded, and the same commit rewrote `recover`'s callsite to discard it. crates/core/src/metadata.rs:3636 | SCOPE | deleting `high_water_marks_refuses_a_segmented_root_rather_than_re_mint_its_chunk_ids` removes a durability guard | Settled at Plan (brief *Scope*, "Delete the standing test with it — and say why in the commit"): the test's hazard needs a minter allocating chunk ids below `2^64`, and neither minter has since `fdd34f1` (#487, 2026-07-08). Its live half — a walk must not silently under-count a record it cannot read — is superseded and strengthened by the totality requirement, bound by `mod startup_recovery` (`metadata.rs:3670`) and end-to-end by `crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs`.
crates/server/src/cli.rs:1983 | SCOPE | a damaged `meta:next_inode` should be repaired automatically (reseeded from the walk's floor) rather than left for an operator | The mirror image of round 6's reversal, and it must be answered with the invariant rather than with convenience: `docs/principles.md` §5 C-1 permits exactly two answers for a record a recovery cannot read — fail closed **for that record**, or contribute its **true** floor. A floor derived from committed `inode:` keys is not the counter's true floor: it says nothing about ids already handed out to an in-flight writer, or ids whose objects were deleted while their fragments are still deadlined under an `orphan:` grace record, and the cluster path derives an object's chunk ids from its inode id (`chunk_id_minter`), so re-minting one of those writes a live object's chunk ids — which `crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs:1107` now demonstrates costs a committed object its bytes, not merely a conflict. A repair that can clobber a committed object's fragments is not a smaller cost than a new-key PUT that refuses.

## Iteration 6 — what changed about the rejections themselves

Round 5's three blocking findings were **fixed, not rejected** (unbounded seed retry, the
unsafe damaged-counter reseed, the lenient `parse_inode_key`) — see `build-notes.md` §1. Two
consequences for this file:

* **One earlier rejection is REVERSED, deliberately and on new evidence** — the iteration-4
  entry at `cli.rs:1851` (reproduced at the bottom of this file) rejected "leave a damaged
  `meta:next_inode` in place and let `alloc_inode` fail closed". That is exactly what this
  round now does. The rejection rested on "the reseed is safe by construction"; round 5's
  review showed the construction proves only that the floor is above every **committed** id,
  while the counter's true value also stands above ids that are **handed out and not
  committed** — an id a peer is mid-PUT with, and an id whose object was deleted while its
  fragments are still deadlined under an `orphan:` grace record. The maintainer's round-5
  carry-forward made it an instruction: *"Needs a reseed strategy that cannot regress below
  any live or in-flight id."* No value derived from committed keys can be **proven** at or
  above an unknowable counter, so the only strategy that cannot regress is not to write one.
  Recorded as a reversal rather than silently dropped: `build-notes.md` §3 states the cost of
  the answer now taken (new-key PUTs fail until the record is repaired; reads, overwrites and
  deletes are unaffected) so the human can weigh it at sign-off.
* **The DST TEST-GAP finding (`cli.rs:1848`/`:1875`) no longer has a subject.** It was raised
  against *the new CAS-based damaged-counter repair path*; this round removes that path. What
  remains at that site is the pre-existing compare-and-set loop from `origin/main`
  (`crates/server/src/cli.rs:1692-1711` on base) plus an attempt **bound**, and the bound is
  itself bound by a test that fails without it
  (`crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs`,
  `recovery_reaches_a_result_over_a_permanently_conflicting_counter`). No new concurrent
  production path ships in this patch.

crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2158 | CONVENTION | The new paged recovery loop awaits each external `scan_page` call without a timeout, violating the repository's rule that every await on external work be bounded and fail closed | Rejected on the tree's own, already-merged answer to this exact question, which stands one screen below this loop **and on `origin/main` before this patch** (`git show origin/main:crates/core/src/metadata.rs`, lines 2142-2149): "The TIME an await may take is the BACKEND's … `wyrd-core` holds no runtime dependency to spend a caller-side deadline from (ADR-0009; `crates/core/Cargo.toml:11-15` keeps core executor-free), and no other metadata call in this module wraps one." The seam assigns the bound to the implementation — "a backend must bound its own waiting rather than block a caller forever on an unreachable cluster" (`crates/traits/src/lib.rs:1000-1002`) — and each networked driver imposes it (`crates/metadata-fdb/src/lib.rs:78-89`, `crates/metadata-tikv/src/lib.rs:143-172`); the embedded backend is synchronous and needs none. The cost of "fixing" it is not a wrapper line: `wyrd-core` has no `tokio` dependency at all, so it would mean taking a runtime dependency in the crate ADR-0009 keeps executor-free, plus a deadline constant this walk would be the only reader of, while `get`/`commit`/`scan_page` everywhere else in the same module stay unwrapped. Same content-stable rejection the brief carries as *Do-not-re-earn* (i): the implementation owns the network bound, not the caller (rejected 3x across #508/#636). The position is written at the loop itself (`metadata.rs:2147-2157`). NOTE the distinction from what this round DID fix: the *retry* loop in `seed_next_inode_floor` had no bound at all and now has one (`cli.rs:1727`, `:1857`) — an unbounded number of awaits is this patch's to fix; the duration of one await is the backend's.
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2169 | CONVENTION | The new metadata-page await has no timeout … allowing a stalled backend to hang startup recovery indefinitely | Same finding as `:2158` above, reported at the await rather than the function; same disposition and the same in-tree citations. On the "hang startup recovery indefinitely" half specifically: the pre-#652 walk had exactly the same exposure through `MetadataStore::scan` (`origin/main:crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2077`, `:2094`, `:2105` — three unbounded awaits, where this patch leaves one), so it is not a hazard the patch introduces; it is the seam's standing contract, unchanged.

Re-deriving a mark with no reader is not a safety property; a finding asking for it must be answered with this decision, not with apparatus.
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2237 | SCOPE | caller-side fan-out timeout | Rejected 3x across #508/#636: the `ChunkStore` implementation owns the network bound, not the caller.
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2237 | SCOPE | retraction of already-published bytes | Rejected 4x in #638 on unchanged evidence.
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:2237 | SCOPE | `Completed` releases its admission slot | Withdrawn as unsatisfiable; a `Completed` tombstone stays counted.
crates/core/src/metadata.rs:3585 | SCOPE | deleting `high_water_marks_refuses_a_segmented_root_rather_than_re_mint_its_chunk_ids` removes a durability guard | Settled at Plan (brief *Scope*, "Delete the standing test with it — and say why in the commit"): the test's hazard needs a minter allocating chunk ids below `2^64`, and neither minter has since `fdd34f1` (#487, 2026-07-08). Its live half — a walk must not silently under-count a record it cannot read — is superseded and strengthened by the totality requirement, bound by `mod startup_recovery` (`metadata.rs:3619-3778`) and end-to-end by `crates/server/tests/gateway_recover_totality.rs`.

## Rejected in iteration 4 (the `meta:next_inode` repair), re-anchored

crates/server/src/cli.rs:1851 | SCOPE | startup recovery should leave a damaged `meta:next_inode` in place (attribute only) and let `alloc_inode` fail closed on it, rather than reseed it | Rejected on the invariant, with the cost stated. "Fail closed for that record" is one of the two legal answers (`docs/principles.md` §5 C-1, the brief's *Invariant to restore*) and it IS the answer `alloc_inode` gives (`cli.rs:1772-1780`) — but at *recovery* it converts a total outage into a permanently write-dead gateway: every new-key PUT fails until a human hand-writes a counter, and the number that human would have to invent is exactly the floor the store's own `inode:` keys already prove. The reseed is safe by construction, not by hope: the floor is `max(inode: key) + 1`, `metadata::create` is `require_absent` on the inode key (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:1571`), so every *committed* object's id is strictly below it and no committed record's id is re-opened — the same construction the legacy absent-counter path (#364 finding 1) has relied on since it landed. See `build-notes.md` §3 for the residual (an id whose object was deleted but whose fragments are still in the orphan ledger), which is identical for the absent-counter path and unchanged by this patch.
